newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold, silver end lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold, silver end lower on profit-taking.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat closes 10 rupes lower at 4,820 rupees per 10 gramme against previous close of 4,830 rupees on demand resistance and light profit-taking.
** Gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) ends 100 rupees lower at 56,400 rupees against previous close of 56,500 rupees per piece.
** Silver (.999) closes 20 rupees lower at 7,450 rupees per kg against the previous close of 7,470 rupees.

Gold 24 carat closed 10 rupees lower at 4,820 rupees per 10 gramme on Wednesday against previous closing of 4,830 rupees as lower than expected seasonal buying prompted profit-taking which trimmed early gains towards the close, dealers said.
Gold opened 15 rupees up at 4,845 rupees per 10 gramme in early trade but later on dropped during the day, they said.
Gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 100 rupees lower at 56,400 rupees per piece against previous closing of 56,500 rupees. They were up by 100 rupees per piece on Tuesday and by 400 rupees on Monday.
Sentiments in the gold market remained subdued at the close amid limited physical enquiries.
Silver (.999) closed 20 rupees lower at 7,450 rupees per kg against previous closing of 7,470 rupees as demand resistance from the industrial buyers and fresh arrivals prompted profit-taking.
Silver was up by 95 rupees per kg on Tuesday. A weak trend in the world market also hurt the sentiments at the close. (Conversion $1=35.84 rupees)
